name: Executive order of January 16, 1879 (Carlin Farms reservation cancelled)
aka: Cancellation of the Carlin Farms reserve
nations: Newe (Western Shoshone), Te-Moak bands, who farmed at Carlin (per the Indian Claims Commission)
The 1877 order names the "Northwestern Shoshone Indians"
promises: This order made no promise. It revoked the order of May 10, 1877 that had set apart the Carlin Farms as a reservation and restored the lands to their original status.
landTaken: The Carlin Farms reservation, about 521.61 acres by the 1877 order, was restored to the public domain (Royce).
today: The Indian Claims Commission, ruling on offsets in the Western Shoshone claim in 1977, found that Western Shoshone had settled and farmed at Carlin, that some refused to move to the Duck Valley reservation created in 1877, and that cattle provided to the Ruby Valley Western Shoshone were moved to Carlin. It recorded Chief Temoak's reply when asked to move there: "If you move my country, I go too. Have my ground here, I can't move." The Commission did not rule on the cancellation itself.

nationVoice.summary: The Tribe says the 1863 Treaty of Ruby Valley granted it ownership of much of eastern Nevada, that settlers took the most fertile Newe lands, that the Bureau of Indian Affairs tried to push all Great Basin Shoshone onto the Duck Valley reservation, and that the tribe refused the $26 million later offered for its land and asked for the land back.

openQuestions: Decided by Jordan 2026-11-08: an executive order taking back executive-order land is not a breach by itself; it needs a finding. this is a reservation revoked by executive order without any record of consent or payment, but no court, Commission, Congress or government admission was found calling it a breach of a treaty, so it stays "no breach found yet". The Ruby Valley treaty of 1863 (Article VI, reservations for the Western Shoshone) is the treaty to research to settle it.
Whether the Western Shoshone award in Docket 326-K (land valued as of July 1, 1872) included the Carlin Farms acreage was not checked.
The order names the "Northwestern Shoshone Indians"; no source was found placing Northwestern Shoshone at Carlin. Nothing from the Fort Bridger or Box Elder treaties is attributed here.
No Te-Moak or other Western Shoshone page about Carlin Farms was found.

2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for Court of Claims "Shoshone" (opened 95 Ct. Cl. 642, 100 Ct. Cl. 455, 103 Ct. Cl. 795, 209 Ct. Cl. 43, 219 Ct. Cl. 346) and ICC full text "Carlin Farms" (OSU 1476 and 2716, already used); nothing new.
